transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. Am I sitting in the right spot? Okay, good. 

Well, I'm here because... it's actually a little embarrassing to admit, to be honest. I hope it's okay to talk about this. I know it probably sounds silly for a grown man, but the thought of getting on an airplane right now just scares me so badly. 

Logically, I know it doesn't make any sense at all. I really do. But whenever I even think about having to fly, my body just... it just tells me that the plane is going to fall out of the sky. I hope I'm explaining that right? I just want to be able to handle it better, if that's something you think you might be able to help me with.
Is your fear mainly about flying, or do you experience similar anxiety in other situations as well, like being in crowded places, public speaking, or other specific triggers?

Oh, no, it's really just the flying. I don't have any trouble with crowds or, um, public speaking or anything like that. I mean, I get normal nerves sometimes, just like anyone else would, I think? But nothing at all like this. It's really just airplanes. 

I hope that's a helpful answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so I'm not wasting your time.
When you think about flying or are in an airplane, do you experience physical symptoms like sweating, trembling, rapid heartbeat, or shortness of breath?

Well... yes. I hope it doesn't make me sound too weak or anything, but, um, yeah, I do get those. 

Actually, it happens even if I'm not anywhere near an airport. Like, if I just get an email at work about covering a rural shift that would need a flight... my heart just starts pounding right away. My hands get all sweaty, and I honestly feel like I cannot breathe until I just close the message and look away. 

I know I shouldn't react that way, and I try to keep it together, but it just hits me so fast. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of details... I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
How long have you felt this way about flying, and do you go out of your way to avoid situations where you might have to be on a plane?

Well, um... I guess it's been about seven months now. I hope that's not too long to have waited to get help? I just thought I could push through it, you know? 

It really started after... well, I lost my job at the clinic I was working at, which was hard enough, and then right around that time I had to take this flight on a really small plane, and it was just terribly turbulent. Ever since then, it's just been this overwhelming fear. 

And as for avoiding it... I try not to let it affect my life too much, I really do. I don't want to be a burden or let anyone down. But, um, yes, I suppose I do go out of my way to avoid it. If there's a drive I can make instead, even if it takes days, I'll do that. I just... I can't bring myself to buy a ticket. I hope you don't think less of me for that? I know it's not very rational for a grown man, let alone a doctor. I just want to be sure I'm giving you the full picture so you can tell me if there's a way to fix this.
Have you ever had a sudden episode of intense fear or discomfort that came out of nowhere and wasn't directly related to thinking about flying, like when you're at home or at work?

Oh, no... no, thankfully nothing like that. I don't just... panic out of nowhere. If I'm at home, or, you know, going about a normal day, I'm completely fine. I'm totally functional, I promise. It really is just tied to the airplanes. 

I hope that makes sense? I don't want you to think I'm completely unstable or losing my grip on everything... I just have this one very specific issue. Am I answering your question the right way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
When you know in advance that you might have to fly, do you feel anxious well before the flight, like days or weeks ahead of time?

Well... yes, I suppose I do. I mean, I try not to dwell on it, I really try to just focus on my work and my patients. But if I know there's a trip coming up... it's like this knot in my stomach that just won't go away. 

Even weeks out, I'll catch myself thinking about it and my chest gets tight. I try to hide it, you know, because I don't want to worry my colleagues or seem unprofessional. I just kind of quietly obsess over the weather forecasts or look up alternative driving routes, even if it's across the country. 

I hope that doesn't sound too ridiculous? I know as a physician I should be able to rationalize this better. I just... I really want to be a good patient for you and give you the right information. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you noticed that your fear of flying has been affecting your ability to work or take on professional responsibilities, especially considering you mentioned being a doctor?

Well, um... I really try my best not to let it interfere, I truly do. I pride myself on being dependable, you know? But... I guess if I'm being completely honest, it has caused a few hiccups. 

I've had to turn down some coverage opportunities because they required flying, which... well, it's cost me some income, and I worry my colleagues might be starting to think I'm not as reliable as I used to be. I hate the thought of letting them down. And, um, I've also had to skip a couple of important professional meetings. I even delayed a trip to see my family recently because I just couldn't bring myself to get on the plane. 

I feel terrible admitting all of this. I know I should be handling things better, especially in my profession. I hope you don't think I'm completely incompetent because of this? I'm really trying to fix it, I promise. Does that answer what you were looking for?

When you're exposed to flight-related situations, like thinking about flying or seeing an airplane, do you ever experience sudden, intense episodes of fear that feel like they come on very quickly and peak within minutes?

Oh, um... no, not like a sudden... explosion of fear or anything. I don't just completely lose control like that, I promise. 

If I see an airplane on TV or, you know, think about an upcoming flight, I definitely get that awful, heavy dread I mentioned earlier. But it doesn't suddenly peak in a few minutes and leave me gasping or anything like that. I try really hard to keep a lid on it. I can usually hold myself together well enough on the outside so people don't notice how much it's bothering me. 

I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I'm not having those kinds of extreme, sudden episodes you're describing. I just get very, very anxious. Is that what you were checking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how this works for me.
When you know you will have to fly in the future, do you find yourself having persistent, excessive worry about the flight for days or weeks beforehand?

Well, um... I know we sort of touched on this just a moment ago, and I really don't want to sound like a broken record or waste your time. But... yes, I suppose I do. 

Like I mentioned, I get that knot in my stomach if I know a trip is coming up. I wouldn't call it "excessive," exactly... I mean, I still go to work and see my patients and try to be as productive as possible. I just... I do think about it a lot, maybe more than I should. I'll catch myself checking the weather or looking at maps for days before I actually have to go anywhere near an airport. 

I try to keep it under control, I really do. I don't want to be a burden or let it consume me. I hope I'm explaining this right? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the way you need me to.
Are there any other situations or places, besides flying, that you actively avoid because you're afraid of having a panic attack or feeling trapped?

Oh, no, definitely not. Um... it's really just the airplanes. I promise I'm completely fine with everything else. 

I don't avoid crowds or elevators or small rooms or anything like that. I go to the clinic every day, I do my rounds... I'm completely comfortable in my normal, day-to-day life. I really don't want you to think I'm just falling apart everywhere or that I can't handle being out and about. I pride myself on being very capable in every other aspect of my life, I truly do. 

I hope that's a good sign? That it's strictly just limited to the flying, I mean. I'm completely fine otherwise. Is that what you were hoping to hear?
